cohort: 30 women 6 weeks postpartum: 10 planned cesarean section, 10 emergency cesarean section, and 10 vaginal delivery
finding: MRI/TVS fusion imaging allows standardized and reproducible identification of the cesarean section scar location and demonstrates reduced vascularization in the scar area compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: MRI/TVS fusion showed significant differences in anterior uterine wall thickness or scar area compared to posterior wall thickness in women with planned and emergency cesarean sections, suggesting differences in scar characteristics based on mode of delivery.
